Settings read from the .abr file: 30 px round computed tip (hardness 100%), spacing 9%; paint dynamics: flow pen pressure.
use_for: pen-driven linework with natural fade
inking with pressure-sensitive flow
avoid: it paints in the current foreground colour (the black in the thumbnail is the renderer's colour, not the preset's)
the taper and fade at the ends in the thumbnail comes from the render's simulated pen pressure; with a mouse the stroke would be uniform
saved with 'use brush size': selecting it may keep your current brush size instead of its stored 30 px (inferred from PGD's earlier renders), so set the size after choosing it
the name says Opacity, but the file stores the pen-pressure control under the key PGD reads as flow: treat the exact label as unverified (inferred)
cards.applies_to: a pixel layer or a layer mask (not a type, shape or smart-object layer); it paints in the current foreground colour at the layer's current opacity
cards.how_to_apply: Already in the live Brushes panel list PGD read from Photoshop: choose 'Hard Round Pressure Opacity' there by name. If it is missing, Brushes panel > panel menu > Import Brushes... and pick <Photoshop 2026 install folder>/Presets/Brushes/Legacy Brushes.abr, group 'Default Brushes'. Script route (as PGD's gallery run did it): Action Manager setd on the application's Brsh property with the .abr as 'T   ' (Appe false replaces the whole Brushes list, true appends), then slct a Brsh reference by index (the preset's position in the loaded list, plus an offset PGD detected from sampled-tip IDs).
cards.notes: Settings (size, spacing, dynamics) read from the shipped .abr file with PGD's structural reader (binary, decoded not string-scraped). PGD thumbnail: the preset stroked along an S-path with simulated pressure, black on white (an applied render, not the preset's own preview). Brush-control names (pen pressure, pen tilt, direction) are PGD's reading of the numeric control codes stored in the file (2 = pen pressure, 3 = pen tilt, 6 = direction); the file itself carries no labels, so tilt and direction readings are inferred. Paint-dynamics labels: PGD's reader maps the file key prVr to flow and opVr to opacity (inferred from the Brush tool options; the file itself does not label them).
